# The permission setting: names, shapes and modes, across the nine sources and the wider field (2026)

Research date: 2026-10-23.

How agent products name and shape the stored setting that decides how tool permission requests are handled, so ZeroSDK's `Settings` schema can name and shape its permission setting by the consensus. Findings only; no recommendation beyond what the counts support.

Sources: the nine (Anomaly OpenCode V2, Claude Agent SDK, Claude Code, Cloudflare Agents, Mastra, OpenAI Agents SDK, OpenAI Codex, Vercel AI SDK, Vercel eve) read from `.generated/sources/` (fetched 2026-10-22; the Claude Code `permission-modes` and `hooks` pages were re-fetched live on 2026-10-23 and match), plus source code where the docs stop. Agent GUIs (Emdash, Superset, Crystal, Nimbalyst, the OpenCode app, T3 Code, CloudCLI, mux, vibe-kanban) and the wider field (VS Code, Zed, Cursor CLI, Letta Code, Warp, Gemini CLI, Cline, Roo Code, GitHub Copilot CLI) are read from their source at a pinned commit or their official docs, 27 products in all. Tags: [Docs], [Source], [Inferred].

`permissions?` is universal (9/9) but mostly prose. As a concept name for the agent-wide setting, "permission mode" appears in 4/9 (Claude Agent SDK, Claude Code, Codex, AI SDK); "approval policy/mode" appears in 7/9 but as a stored key only in Codex (`approval_policy`) and, through community providers, the AI SDK docs.

## 1. Field name

The stored setting, by meaning: what an agent-wide (or session-wide) choice of "how tool permission requests are handled" is called. Per-tool flags are listed so the count is honest about sources that have nothing wider.

Count by meaning, over the nine:

- An agent- or session-wide setting exists in 6/9 (OpenCode, Agent SDK, Claude Code, Mastra, Codex, AI SDK). The other 3/9 (Cloudflare, OpenAI Agents SDK, eve) gate per tool only.
- Its key carries "permission": 5/9 (OpenCode `permissions`/`session.permissions`, Agent SDK `permissionMode`, Claude Code `permissions`/`permissionMode`, Mastra `session.permissions`, AI SDK `permissionMode`). Codex makes 6/9 if its UI name "permission mode" and `default_permissions` count, but its approval key is `approval_policy`.
- `permissionMode` exactly: 3/9 (Agent SDK, Claude Code subagents, AI SDK).
- `permissions` as the stored key: 3/9 (OpenCode, Claude Code, Mastra).
- `defaultMode`: 1/9 (Claude Code; the Agent SDK reads the same settings key).
- `approval_policy`/`approvalPolicy`: 1/9 (Codex; the OpenAI Agents SDK only forwards it to its `codexTool`).
- `toolPermissions`, `runtimeMode`, `approvalMode`: 0/9 as a stored key.

## 2. Shape

### The nine

| Product           | Shape                                                                                                                                                                  | Mode key inside the object      | Quote                                                                                                                                                                                       | Link                                                               |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| OpenCode          | rules only: `permissions` is an ordered array of `{ action, resource, effect }`; the TUI's `session.permissions` is a separate two-value enum in another file          | none (no mode in `permissions`) | "Each rule requires three string fields" / "If no rule matches, OpenCode uses `ask`." [Docs]                                                                                                | https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/permissions/                           |
| Claude Agent SDK  | flat options: `permissionMode` enum beside `allowedTools`/`disallowedTools` and `canUseTool`                                                                           | n/a (top-level option)          | "`allowed_tools` and `disallowed_tools` (TypeScript: `allowedTools` / `disallowedTools`) add entries to the allow and deny rule lists" [Docs]                                               | https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions              |
| Claude Code       | object holding the mode and the rule lists                                                                                                                             | `defaultMode`                   | "**Type**: object with `allow`, `ask`, `deny`, `additionalDirectories`, `blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories`, `defaultMode`, `disableBypassPermissionsMode`, and `disableAutoMode`" [Docs] | https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#permissions     |
| Cloudflare Agents | per-tool boolean or function                                                                                                                                           | n/a                             | as above                                                                                                                                                                                    | https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/harnesses/think/tools/    |
| Mastra            | rules only: `{ categories: {...}, tools: {...} }` of policies                                                                                                          | none                            | "`// { categories: { execute: 'ask' }, tools: { dangerous_tool: 'deny' } }`" [Docs]                                                                                                         | https://mastra.ai/reference/agent-controller/session               |
| OpenAI Agents SDK | per-tool boolean or function                                                                                                                                           | n/a                             | as above                                                                                                                                                                                    | https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/human-in-the-loop |
| Codex             | flat top-level keys: `approval_policy` enum (or a `granular` object of category booleans), `approvals_reviewer`, `sandbox_mode`; rules live in separate `.rules` files | n/a                             | "Codex security controls come from two layers ... **Sandbox mode** ... **Approval policy**" [Docs]                                                                                          | https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-approvals-security            |
| Vercel AI SDK     | flat options: `permissionMode` enum beside `activeTools`/`inactiveTools` and `toolApproval`                                                                            | n/a                             | "Harnesses distinguish built-in tool permissions from host-executed tool approvals." [Docs]                                                                                                 | https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/ai-sdk-harnesses/tools                     |
| eve               | per-tool helper                                                                                                                                                        | n/a                             | as above                                                                                                                                                                                    | https://eve.dev/docs/tools                                         |

Of the 6/9 with a wide setting: a single mode enum kept apart from the rules in 3 (Agent SDK, Codex, AI SDK); rules only, no mode, in 2 (OpenCode, whose TUI adds a separate two-value toggle, and Mastra); one object holding both a mode and the rule lists in 1 (Claude Code). The only mode key inside such an object among the nine is `defaultMode`.

Across all 27: a single enum with rules elsewhere (or none) in 9 (Agent SDK, Codex, AI SDK, Superset, Crystal, T3 Code, VS Code, Cursor, Gemini); an object holding a mode key in 4 (Claude Code `defaultMode`, Zed `default`, Letta `mode`, Nimbalyst `permissionMode`), of which 3 also hold the rule lists (Claude Code, Zed, Letta); rules only in 2 (OpenCode, Mastra); booleans in 5 (Emdash, OpenCode app, vibe-kanban, Cline, Roo); one enum per action in 1 (Warp); per-tool only in 3 (Cloudflare, OpenAI Agents SDK, eve); none stored in 2 (mux, Copilot). The mode key inside an object has no majority: `defaultMode`, `default`, `mode` and `permissionMode` once each.

## 3. Mode values by meaning

Meanings: (a) ask the human every time; (b) allow what saved rules allow, ask about the rest; (c) allow everything; (d) a model or classifier decides; (e) auto-accept file edits only; (f) plan or read-only; (g) deny unless pre-approved.

### The nine

| Product           | (a) ask                                                | (b) rules, then ask                            | (c) allow all                                                          | (d) model decides                                             | (e) edits only                                                                      | (f) plan / read-only                                                        | (g) deny unless pre-approved                                             |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| OpenCode          | TUI `prompt`; rule `ask`                               | `prompt` plus rules (no separate value)        | TUI `autoaccept`                                                       | none                                                          | none                                                                                | `plan` is an agent, not a permission value                                  | none as a mode (`deny` rules)                                            |
| Claude Agent SDK  | `default`                                              | `default` plus allow rules (no separate value) | `bypassPermissions`                                                    | `auto`                                                        | `acceptEdits`                                                                       | `plan`                                                                      | `dontAsk`                                                                |
| Claude Code       | `default` (label Manual, alias `manual`)               | `default` plus allow rules (no separate value) | `bypassPermissions`                                                    | `auto`                                                        | `acceptEdits`                                                                       | `plan`                                                                      | `dontAsk`                                                                |
| Cloudflare Agents | `needsApproval: true`                                  | none                                           | `needsApproval: false`                                                 | none                                                          | none                                                                                | none                                                                        | none                                                                     |
| Mastra            | policy `ask`                                           | category/tool policies (no separate value)     | policy `allow`                                                         | none                                                          | none                                                                                | plan is an agent mode (`session.mode`), not a permission value              | policy `deny`                                                            |
| OpenAI Agents SDK | `needsApproval: true`; MCP `requireApproval: 'always'` | none                                           | MCP `requireApproval: 'never'`                                         | none                                                          | none                                                                                | none                                                                        | none                                                                     |
| Codex             | `on-request` (label "Ask for approval")                | `on-request` plus `.rules` (no separate value) | `never` with `danger-full-access` (label "Full access", flag `--yolo`) | `approvals_reviewer = "auto_review"` (label "Approve for me") | none (the `workspace-write` sandbox lets edits inside the workspace run) [Inferred] | sandbox `read-only` / profile `:read-only`; `/plan` is a separate plan mode | `never` with a sandbox; `granular` categories set to `false` auto-reject |
| Vercel AI SDK     | `allow-reads` (mapped to Claude `default`, see below)  | none                                           | `allow-all` (default)                                                  | none                                                          | `allow-edits`                                                                       | none                                                                        | `toolApproval` OPA default `'denied'` ("hard allowlist mode")            |

"`plan` \| Reads, plus classifier-approved commands when auto mode is available" ... "`auto` \| Everything, with background safety checks" ... "`dontAsk` \| File reads inside your working directories and pre-approved tools; anything that would prompt is denied" ... "`bypassPermissions` \| Everything" [Docs] https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#available-modes
- Claude Code: "The mode that reviews every action is named **Manual** in the CLI ... Its config value is `default`, which is what hooks and SDK integrations use. The CLI accepts `manual` as an alias" [Docs] same page.
- Claude Code, (a) and (b) are one mode: "Modes set the baseline. Layer permission rules on top to pre-approve or block specific tools." [Docs] same page.
- Agent SDK: `type PermissionMode = "default" | "acceptEdits" | "bypassPermissions" | "plan" | "dontAsk" | "auto"` with comments "Don't prompt for permissions, deny if not pre-approved" and "A model classifier reviews actions" [Docs] https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#permissionmode

- AI SDK: "`allow-all`: allow built-in reads, edits, and shell commands. Its Claude Code bridge maps them onto Claude's own modes: `permissionMode === 'allow-all' ? 'bypassPermissions' : permissionMode === 'allow-edits' ? 'acceptEdits' : 'default'` [Source] https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/e623e8c88b55066dde769614a16ae51d424974aa/packages/harness-claude-code/src/bridge/index.ts#L176-L190

### The nine

## 6. Fit with ADR 0006

ADR 0006: agents run in Claude's `default` (Manual) mode and the server answers every `PermissionRequest` hook by the main agent's flipper. The question per Claude mode: can the server carry the mode out by how it answers, or must Claude itself run in that mode?

Facts the answers rest on, all [Docs]:

- The hook fires only where Claude would prompt: "PermissionRequest hooks run only when Claude Code is about to ask you for permission, or when it would otherwise auto-deny a call that can't prompt." https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#permissionrequest
- Some actions prompt in every mode: "Claude Code doesn't auto-approve the following in any mode, including `bypassPermissions`": explicit ask rules, connector tools an organization set to `ask`, tools that require user interaction (`AskUserQuestion` and MCP tools marked `requiresUserInteraction`), recognized `rm` and `rmdir` critical-path removals, the cross-session messaging safeguards, and reads outside the working directories while `permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories` is on [Docs] https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#actions-no-mode-auto-approves
- A hook's allow does not beat Claude's own rules: "`behavior` \| `"allow"` grants the permission, `"deny"` denies it. Deny and ask rules are still evaluated, so a hook returning `"allow"` doesn't override a matching deny rule" (same page).
- Calls Claude's own `permissions.allow` rules or the mode already approve never reach the hook: in Manual mode only "Reads only" run without asking, and "Modes set the baseline. Layer permission rules on top to pre-approve or block specific tools." https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes
- A hook can change Claude's mode, but only while allowing a request: "`updatedPermissions` \| For `"allow"` only: array of permission update entries to apply, such as adding an allow rule or changing the session permission mode"; "`setMode` \| `mode`, `destination` \| Changes the permission mode. Valid modes are `default`, `auto`, `acceptEdits`, `dontAsk`, `bypassPermissions`, `plan`, and `manual`"; "`setMode` with `bypassPermissions` only takes effect if you launched the session with bypass mode already available ... Otherwise the update is a no-op." https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#permission-update-entries
- "In modes that ask, a `PermissionRequest` hook can answer the prompt." (said of critical-path removals) https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#critical-path-removals-in-each-permission-mode

| Claude mode         | Can the server carry it out while Claude stays in `default`?                                                 | Why                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Evidence                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `default` (Manual)  | Yes, natively. This is ADR 0006's base                                                                       | Every call that would prompt reaches the hook. Calls already allowed by Claude's own allow rules or its read-only set never reach the server, so "Ask me" cannot ask about them [Inferred]                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | hook quotes above                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `acceptEdits`       | Approximately. Allow Edit/Write/NotebookEdit and the filesystem commands on in-scope paths, forward the rest | To match exactly, the server would have to copy Claude's scope rules: working directory and `additionalDirectories`, wrapper and env-prefix parsing, the symlink check, and the protected and critical paths that still prompt in `acceptEdits` [Inferred]                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | "`acceptEdits` mode auto-approves common filesystem Bash commands: `mkdir`, `touch`, `rm`, `rmdir`, `mv`, `cp`, and `sed` ... auto-approval applies only to paths inside your working directory or `additionalDirectories`." https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#auto-approve-file-edits-with-acceptedits-mode                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `plan`              | No. Claude has to run in `plan`                                                                              | Plan mode changes what Claude is told and adds a plan-approval step (ExitPlanMode), not only which calls are approved. A server that denies every write in `default` gives a read-only agent that was never asked to plan [Inferred]. A hook `setMode: plan` (on an allow) or `--permission-mode plan` puts Claude in it                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | "Plan mode tells Claude to research and propose changes without making them." https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#analyze-before-you-edit-with-plan-mode ; `planModeInstructions`: "The CLI still wraps it with the read-only enforcement preamble and the ExitPlanMode protocol footer" https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript ; "In plan mode, apart from `ExitPlanMode`, your `PreToolUse` hook's `"allow"` has no effect on a file edit" https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#hook-approvals-in-plan-mode |
| `auto`              | No. Claude has to run in `auto`                                                                              | The classifier is Claude Code's own: it reads the transcript, drops broad allow rules on entry, and reviews subagent spawns and reports. In `default`, requests reach the hook with no classifier verdict. A server could run its own reviewer model, as Codex `auto_review` and eve `auto()` do, but that is not Claude's auto mode [Inferred]. Under `auto`, the server still sees what the classifier does not settle (ask rules, critical-path removals, the fallback after repeated blocks) and denials arrive on `PermissionDenied` | "In auto mode, a second model, the classifier, reviews actions instead of you" https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes ; "`PermissionDenied` ... Runs when auto mode denies a tool call ... This hook only fires in auto mode" https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#permissiondenied                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `dontAsk`           | Yes: answer `deny` to every request                                                                          | The hook fires exactly for the calls that would prompt, which are the ones `dontAsk` auto-denies [Inferred]. The difference: `dontAsk` also denies `AskUserQuestion`, which under ADR 0006 the server answers through `PreToolUse` instead                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | "If you set `dontAsk` mode, Claude Code auto-denies every tool call that would otherwise prompt you" https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#allow-only-pre-approved-tools-with-dontask-mode                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `bypassPermissions` | Approximately: answer `allow` to every request (ADR 0006's "Allow all")                                      | Same outcome for ordinary calls, plus every call passes the server and is recorded. Differences: deny rules still win over a hook allow (they also win in `bypassPermissions`); explicit ask rules prompt in both; a hook can answer the critical-path prompt that `bypassPermissions` still shows [Inferred]. The real mode cannot be switched to by hook unless the session launched with it, and ADR 0006 rejected it because "no request ever reaches the server"                                                                     | "Deny rules block in every mode, including `bypassPermissions`." https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes ; ADR 0006 Considered Options                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

So 4/6 of Claude's modes can be carried out by a server answering `PermissionRequest` while Claude stays in `default` (`default` exactly, `dontAsk` almost exactly, `bypassPermissions` and `acceptEdits` approximately), and 2/6 need Claude itself in the mode (`auto`, `plan`).

Precedent from the nine: the AI SDK drives Claude Code through a bridge and does both. Its Claude bridge sets Claude's own mode (`allow-all` → `bypassPermissions`, `allow-edits` → `acceptEdits`, `allow-reads` → `default`), adds `permissions.ask` rules, and answers the remaining prompts through `canUseTool` [Source] https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/e623e8c88b55066dde769614a16ae51d424974aa/packages/harness-claude-code/src/bridge/index.ts#L176-L230 . Its ACP adapter either sets the harness's own session mode or, with no mapping, answers the requests itself: "When omitted, the adapter applies `permissionMode` to ACP permission requests by tool kind." [Docs] https://ai-sdk.dev/providers/ai-sdk-harnesses/acp

Counts over the GUIs that drive Claude: every one that offers plan runs Claude in its own `plan` (5/5: Superset, T3 Code, CloudCLI, Nimbalyst, vibe-kanban), and every one that offers a classifier mode runs Claude's own `auto` (4/4: Superset, T3 Code, CloudCLI, Nimbalyst). Accept-edits: 3 set Claude's `acceptEdits` (Superset, T3 Code, CloudCLI) and 1 emulates it in its hook (Nimbalyst). Allow-all: every GUI that offers it can launch Claude with `bypassPermissions` or `--dangerously-skip-permissions` (8/8); Nimbalyst's hook path also emulates it. Answering requests themselves: all 8 GUIs with a setting do so on at least one path (`canUseTool`, a `--permission-prompt-tool`, a `PreToolUse` hook, ACP `requestPermission`, or OpenCode's `reply`); Emdash's terminal mode and Superset's terminal presets only pass a flag.

Nimbalyst's hook path is the closest match to ADR 0006 (Claude kept in `default`, the app answers): it carries allow-all and accept-edits itself and hands `plan` and `auto` to Claude. That matches the 4/6 and 2/6 split above.

## Consensus

Counts give the nine first, then all 27 products (the nine, 9 agent GUIs, 9 from the wider field). "Majority" means more than half; otherwise the leader is called a plurality.

| Question                         | Majority answer                                                                 | Counts                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Claude's answer                                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1. Field name                    | The key contains "permission(s)"                                                | Nine 5/9; all 15/27. No exact key has a majority: `permissionMode` (or `defaultPermissionMode`/`PermissionMode`) 7/27 (Agent SDK, Claude Code, AI SDK, Crystal, Nimbalyst, CloudCLI, Letta) leads; an approval-rooted key 8/27 (Codex `approval_policy`, Cursor `approvalMode`, Gemini `defaultApprovalMode`, Cline, Roo, Emdash, OpenCode app, vibe-kanban); `defaultMode` 1/27; `tool_permissions` 1/27; `runtimeMode` 1/27. As a concept name, "permission mode" is used by 4/9 of the nine (term counter). 3/9 of the nine have no agent-wide setting at all (per-tool gates only) | `permissions` holds it, with the mode at `permissions.defaultMode`; agents and the SDK use `permissionMode`                                                                            |
| 2. Shape                         | None. Plurality: a single mode enum, with any rule lists kept elsewhere         | Single enum 9/27 (nine: 3/9). An object holding a mode key 4/27, 3 of them with the rule lists inside (Claude Code, Zed, Letta; nine: 1/9). Booleans 5/27, rules only 2/27, one enum per action 1/27, per tool only 3/27, nothing stored 2/27. The mode key inside an object has no majority: `defaultMode` (Claude Code), `default` (Zed), `mode` (Letta), `permissionMode` (Nimbalyst), once each                                                                                                                                                                                    | An object `permissions` holding `defaultMode` plus `allow`/`ask`/`deny`                                                                                                                |
| 3a. Ask (the prompting baseline) | Plurality `default`                                                             | `default` 7 of the 20 products with an enum (Claude Code, Agent SDK, Superset, CloudCLI, VS Code, Gemini, Copilot). "ask" roots the stored value in 4 (OpenCode, Mastra, Nimbalyst, Warp `AlwaysAsk`) and the UI label in 4 more (Codex and Superset "Ask for approval", vibe-kanban "Ask", Cursor's deprecated "Ask Every Time"). The label "Manual" appears in 3 (Claude Code, Crystal, VS Code `manual`)                                                                                                                                                                            | `default`, labelled Manual, alias `manual`                                                                                                                                             |
| 3b. Rules, then ask              | Folded into (a)                                                                 | A separate value exists in only 2/27 (Letta `standard`, Cursor `allowlist`), 0/9 in the nine. Everyone else, Claude included, applies saved rules on top of the ask value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | folded into `default`                                                                                                                                                                  |
| 3c. Allow all                    | None                                                                            | "allow" roots 6 (`allow`, `allowAll`, `allow-all`, `AlwaysAllow`), "bypass" roots 5 (`bypassPermissions` 4, all Claude or Claude wrappers, plus `bypass-all`), `unrestricted` 2, `never` 2, `full-access` 1 (the label "Full access" in 3). `yolo` is a stored value only in Gemini but a flag or command alias in 7. It is the shipped default in 5/9 GUIs                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | `bypassPermissions`                                                                                                                                                                    |
| 3d. Claude itself: `auto` (Claude's classifier) and `plan` (Claude's planning instructions and ExitPlanMode). The GUIs agree: 5/5 offering plan and 4/4 offering auto run Claude in that mode; accept-edits is native in 3/4 and emulated in 1/4. A hook can switch Claude's mode only while allowing a request (`setMode`), and never into `bypassPermissions` unless the session launched with it                                              | n/a                                                                                                                                                                                    |

The counts bear on ADR 0006's flipper in three ways, without going further. Its three choices cover meanings (a), (b) and (c). Only 2/27 products give (b) a value of its own; the rest, Claude included, fold saved rules into (a). Claude's own word for (a) is `default`, which is also the plurality name. Of the meanings the flipper lacks, `auto` has a majority name; `acceptEdits` and `plan` lead their meanings; and `plan` is kept off the permission setting by most products.
